_comment: Chapter 08's reviewed scope for the fictional contoso.example tenant: which service principals CA015 and CA037 cover, in which ring, the workload egress ranges (documentation ranges from RFC 5737 and RFC 3849, never real ones), the identities out of scope with the control that covers each instead, and the enforcement record. A real tenant keeps its own copy beside its decision records; every change is a reviewed pull request.

licensing.outcome: License the Tier 1 single-tenant service principals

outOfScope.name: vm-batch01
outOfScope.control: Not covered by Conditional Access (Learn). Azure role assignments scoped to the resource (Chapter 07) and an access review of the identity (Learn suggests one for managed identities)

outOfScope.name: id-deploy
outOfScope.control: Not covered by Conditional Access (Learn). Federated credential limited to one repository and branch (Chapter 05); role assignments scoped to the resource group (Chapter 07)

outOfScope.name: Partner CRM
outOfScope.control: A third party's multitenant app: admin consent review of its permissions and the quarterly owner review (Chapter 07); ID Protection still detects risk on it (Learn)

outOfScope.name: Vendor Portal
outOfScope.control: Registered here but multitenant: Chapter 03's disposition re-registers it single-tenant, then it joins Ring2

outOfScope.name: Benefits Q&A Agent
outOfScope.control: An AI agent identity: Chapter 09's controls; agent Conditional Access is preview and stays a watch item

outOfScope.name: Old SAML Connector
outOfScope.control: A legacy service principal with no registration: Chapter 02's orphan rule, then retirement
